items.q: Why is my GoHighLevel missed call text back not sending?
items.a:
Work through three checks. First, the setting: HighLevel sends nothing unless Missed Call Text Back is enabled under Settings, Phone System, Voice, and only a call that rings past the incoming call timeout counts as missed, so an answered call never triggers it.

Second, the sending number. A local number needs the green A2P Verified label under Settings, Phone System, Phone Numbers. HighLevel's error guide says error 30034 means the number is not fully registered for A2P: link it to the approved campaign and allow up to 24 hours after approval for carrier activation. A Sole Proprietor registration supports one local number per campaign. A toll-free number fails with error 30032 until its verification is approved.

Third, the contact: a caller who replied STOP or has SMS Do Not Disturb switched on is skipped. When a text does fail, the contact's conversation marks it Unsuccessful, and the red warning beside it shows the error code.

items.q: Why did my GoHighLevel missed call text come from a different number?
items.a:
Because the number the caller dialed could not send texts. HighLevel's Missed Call Text Back article says the feature tries the dialed number first and, when that number is not eligible to send SMS, falls back in a fixed order: a number that has already texted the contact successfully, then the location's default outbound number, then any other eligible number in the location. Call tracking numbers, number pools and toll-free numbers that have not passed verification are the examples HighLevel gives, since they can take calls without being cleared to send texts.

Nothing needs switching on, because the fallback is automatic whenever the feature is enabled. The catch is recognition: a customer may not link a text from an unfamiliar number to the business they just rang, so put the business name in the first words of the message. A fallback text is billed like any other, at $0.00747 per segment plus the carrier fee.

items.q: How do I stop GoHighLevel texting the same caller several times?
items.a:
Replace the Settings switch with a workflow. HighLevel's Missed Call Text Back article says the switch sends a text for every missed call, even when one person rings several times in a short space of time, and it recommends customizing the missed-call recipe in Workflows instead. Its suggestions are a wait step of around 20 minutes, or tags such as 1st call and 2nd call that let the workflow treat repeat attempts differently.

HighLevel's article on the Call Status trigger, which it now titles Call details, adds that the trigger fires on each status change of a call, so add a condition or cooldown that lets each caller through once. When the workflow is live, turn the Settings switch off: HighLevel's WhatsApp equivalent lists overlapping text-back settings and workflows as a cause of duplicate messages. Every duplicate that gets through costs $0.00747 per segment plus the carrier fee.

items.q: Can GoHighLevel missed call text back work with my existing business number?
items.a:
Yes, as long as calls to that number reach HighLevel's phone system, which happens when your carrier forwards them to a GoHighLevel number or when you port the number itself into HighLevel. HighLevel's call forwarding article gives carrier codes for forwarding only unanswered and busy calls: *71 followed by the HighLevel number on Verizon Wireless, Xfinity Mobile and Spectrum Mobile, and **61*1 plus the number and # on T-Mobile. Its Google Business Profile integration takes another route, putting the HighLevel number in the listing's primary slot, moving your existing number to the secondary slot and passing calls through to it.

Keeping your own number has a long-term advantage, since HighLevel's Terms release numbers bought through the platform within 14 days of cancellation. Test with a call from another phone, and avoid two numbers that forward to each other. The HighLevel number costs $1.15 a month, and each minute HighLevel forwards to another US number costs $0.02.

items.q: Can I use a toll-free number for missed call text back in GoHighLevel?
items.a:
Yes, once the number has passed toll-free verification. HighLevel's A2P campaign guide describes toll-free messaging as a separate verification process that does not rely on A2P 10DLC brand and campaign registration, and its error guide says texts from an unverified toll-free number fail with error 30032. Until verification is approved, Missed Call Text Back does not simply give up: HighLevel's article says it sends from another eligible number in the location, such as an A2P-verified local number, when one exists.

On GoHighLevel's phone system, toll-free numbers rent at $2.15 a month against $1.15 for local ones, and each incoming minute on a toll-free number costs $0.0198 rather than $0.01165. The per-segment rate for texts is the same $0.00747 on both number types, though HighLevel's cost article notes that carrier fees vary by number type.

items.q: What should a missed call text back message say?
items.a:
Name the business first, acknowledge the missed call and offer one next step, all within 160 plain characters so the text bills as a single segment. HighLevel's prefilled message for the WhatsApp version follows that pattern: it gives the location's name, says the business just missed the call and asks how it can help.

Three GoHighLevel details shape the wording. Any emoji switches the text to Unicode, which fits only 70 characters per segment. A merge field for the caller's name fills in only when HighLevel already knows the contact, so the message has to read naturally without it. And HighLevel's A2P campaign guide wants sample messages that identify the sender and include opt-out wording, so ending with a line such as "Reply STOP to opt out" keeps the live text in line with what you registered. If the message carries a booking link, declare links in the campaign's message details.

items.q: Can GoHighLevel reply to missed calls on WhatsApp instead of SMS?
items.a:
Yes. HighLevel has a separate Missed Call WhatsApp Back setting in the same place as the SMS one, under Settings, Phone System, Voice, then Voicemail & Missed Call Text Back. It needs a WhatsApp-enabled number connected to the sub-account, and the message arrives only if the caller uses WhatsApp, so HighLevel suggests keeping the SMS version or a fallback workflow for everyone else.

The WhatsApp integration is billed at $10 a month per sub-account where it is switched on, plus a charge for each delivered message that varies with the country and the message category; in the US, a utility template costs $0.0036 and a marketing template $0.0263. HighLevel's missed-call WhatsApp article does not say which category its message counts as. Pick one channel as the main reply, because HighLevel's troubleshooting list points to overlapping SMS text-back or workflows when the same caller gets duplicate messages.
